description: Passionate about self-development, artificial intelligence, Python programming, and academic research. Seeking teammates skilled in data processing, machine learning, or practical prototyping for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. If our interests align, let's connect and build something impactful.
summary: For 25 years aboard the International Space Station, shutting down ventilation fans has been the standard response to cabin fires. However, lunar habitats introduce a dangerous paradox: reduced gravity (1/6 g), lower pressure (56.5 kPa), and higher oxygen (34%) create a natural buoyant draft that keeps flames burning even when fans are off.   To address this challenge, we developed lunar-flame-dynamics PSI, an interactive web platform integrated with a real-time sensor AI model. Built around 24 investigations from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database, our hands-on virtual combustion lab lets users mount spacecraft materials, ignite samples, move an interactive probe across the flame to read local temperature and oxygen, switch to Thermal IR to spot invisible 600K cool flames, and summarize, rank, and compare all 24 studies.   To guide astronauts and engineers directly, the platform features two intelligent tools: a bilingual Q&A chatbot (SI Interpreter) that answers user questions using live chamber data and NASA records, and an Edge-AI Random Forest model that reads live cabin sensors to predict the exact fire scenario and recommend immediate, actionable suppression steps.
details: We developed lunar-flame-dynamics PSI, an interactive space fire-safety platform that combines a 5-step virtual combustion laboratory on the web with a real-time Edge-AI sensor model on Google Colab. Instead of building a static data table, we created a hands-on workbench where users first test a side-by-side fire simulation comparing zero gravity on the Space Station (0 g) with lunar gravity on the Moon (1/6 g) at 34% oxygen and 56.5 kPa (8.2 psi) an atmosphere chosen so astronauts can use 4.3 psi pure-oxygen spacesuits without hours of pre-breathing to avoid decompression sickness proving that cutting the ventilation fans starves a fire in orbit, whereas lunar buoyancy creates a 6.4 cm/s upward draft that keeps the flame burning. Across the 5-step lab, users mount four spacecraft specimens (Cast Acrylic PMMA windows, Cotton-fiberglass SIBAL fabric, a 3mm Lithium battery gap, or Nomex shielding), lock in a scientific hypothesis, ignite the sample, move an interactive probe across the flame to read local temperature (K) and oxygen levels, switch to a Thermal IR camera to spot invisible 600K cool flames, pin up to six experimental trials onto a live curve, and test nitrogen purge and 20-micron water-mist suppression across four lunar base and rover zones. To directly fulfill the challenge goals, users filter, rank, and compare all 24 NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) investigations (20 orbital flight studies across CIR, MDCA, MSG, and Cygnus, plus 4 PSI-based ground modeling studies) using an explainable Evidence Fit Score out of 100, verified PSI/DOI links, and a Partial-Gravity Bounding Envelope (0 g to 1 g) with CSV upload support for future LUCI and FM2 lunar flight data, while clearly separating educational model estimates from raw NASA flight records. Finally, to bridge the gap between engineering research and emergency response, our platform features two intelligent tools that benefit both space missions and Earth industries (preventing EV battery thermal runaway, protecting hospital ICUs with fine water mist, separating 0.18-micron fire smoke from >2-micron mine and lunar dust via SAME and DAFT findings, and improving firefighter gear): a bilingual (English/Arabic) Q&A chatbot (SI Interpreter) that answers user questions by linking live chamber telemetry to the 24 NASA studies, and a Random Forest Edge-AI model on Google Colab (built with Python, Scikit-learn, NumPy, Pandas, and Gradio alongside our HTML5, CSS3, ES6 JavaScript, Canvas, SVG, and localStorage web app on GitHub Pages) that reads five live cabin sensors (oxygen, nitrogen, pressure, airflow, and gravity) to predict the exact upcoming fire scenario in milliseconds and recommend immediate, actionable suppression steps for a wearable spacesuit chip.zPSI, an interactive space fire-safety platform that combines a 5-step virtual combustion laboratory on the web with a real-time Edge-AI sensor model on Google Colab.
